title: Signature Trace-to-Test Pipeline
description: Signature edition: every violation trace the model checker finds is automatically converted into a regression test against the real implementation. The abstract bug becomes a concrete test that fails until the implementation is fixed — formal findings never die in a report. This is a Signature original method.
method: Translate the checker's trace to implementation-level steps; emit a test; run against the implementation; keep the test as a permanent regression guard.
usage: Wire trace conversion into the checking pipeline; never close a finding without its regression test.

demo.code:
print('trace: 7 steps -> test_consensus_no_split_brain.py generated')
print('test FAILS on current impl -> fix -> test PASSES (guard kept)')

title: Signature Symbolic model checking with BDDs
description: Signature edition: Symbolic model checking represents sets of states as Binary Decision Diagrams instead of enumerating them, checking hardware-scale state spaces (10^100+) that explicit enumeration could never touch. NuSMV pioneered it for hardware and protocol verification.
method: Encode the system symbolically; represent state sets as BDDs; compute fixpoints for CTL properties; BDD variable ordering is the performance key.
usage: Order BDD variables by dependency; abstract aggressively; use for control-heavy hardware and protocols.

demo.code:
print('NuSMV: symbolic check of arbiter, 2^64 states')
print('AG(req -> AF grant): TRUE (BDD fixpoint converged)')

title: Signature State-space hashing and compression
description: Signature edition: Explicit-state checkers store billions of visited states; bitstate hashing and collapse compression shrink each state to bits, trading a tiny probability of hash collision for 10-100x memory savings. SPIN's bitstate mode checks enormous spaces on ordinary machines.
method: Hash states into a bit array (bitstate) or compress common prefixes (collapse); accept the quantified collision risk; verify critical results with exact mode.
usage: Use approximate modes for bug hunting, exact mode for final certification of critical properties.

demo.code:
print('bitstate: 2^27 bits covers 4.1B-state space in 16MB')
print('collision risk < 1e-6 -> acceptable for bug hunting')

title: Signature Counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR)
description: Signature edition: CEGAR starts with a coarse abstraction of the system; if the abstract check finds a violation, it tests whether the counterexample is real — spurious ones refine the abstraction, real ones are reported. The abstraction grows only as precise as needed, automatically.
method: Abstract -> model check -> validate counterexample -> refine on spurious -> repeat; SLAM/SDV applied this to Windows drivers.
usage: Use for software with huge concrete state spaces; let refinement be driven by spurious counterexamples.

demo.code:
print('CEGAR iteration 3: spurious cex -> predicate added')
print('iteration 4: abstract check PASSES -> property holds')

title: Signature Assume-guarantee compositional checking
description: Signature edition: Checking a whole system at once doesn't scale; assume-guarantee splits it: prove each component correct assuming its environment meets an interface contract, then check the contracts compose. Components are checked once, in isolation, and the composition proof is small.
method: Specify assume/guarantee contracts per component; model-check each against its contract; verify contract compatibility at composition.
usage: Invest in good interface contracts; they're the reusable asset across component versions.

demo.code:
print('component A: proved under assume(env fair)')
print('component B: guarantees fairness -> contracts compose: SYSTEM HOLDS')

title: Signature Model checking in CI pipelines
description: Signature edition: Model checking earns its keep when it runs on every change: specs live next to code, the checker runs in CI with bounded scopes, and regressions in the design fail the build like test failures. Amazon's TLA+ CI integration is the template — formal specs as living CI artifacts.
method: Check in specs + models; CI runs the checker with fixed bounds/seeds; failures block merge; bound increases are deliberate decisions.
usage: Keep check times CI-friendly (bound the model); treat spec failures as design bugs, not noise.

demo.code:
print('CI: TLC check, bound 4, seed 42 -> 88,231 states, 0 violations (41s)')
print('spec regression: none -> MERGE')

title: Signature Partial-order reduction
description: Signature edition: Concurrent systems explode combinatorially because independent actions interleave. Partial-order reduction observes that independent actions commute, so the checker explores one representative interleaving per equivalence class — often shrinking the state space by orders of magnitude without losing bugs.
method: Compute action independence; explore ample/persistent sets; preserve at least one interleaving per Mazurkiewicz trace.
usage: Enable POR in the checker; define independence accurately (wrong independence = missed bugs).

demo.code:
print('without POR: 48M states; with POR: 1.2M states')
print('same bugs found — 40x reduction')

title: Signature TLA+ specification checking (TLC)
description: Signature edition: TLA+ lets engineers write precise specs of distributed systems, and the TLC model checker explores all behaviors up to a bound. Amazon famously used TLA+ to find deep bugs in DynamoDB and S3 designs before coding — spec-level model checking catching what testing never would.
method: Write the spec in TLA+; define the model (constants, bounds); TLC enumerates behaviors; invariant violations produce minimal traces.
usage: Spec the tricky coordination logic; bound the model to check; turn violation traces into regression tests.

demo.code:
print('TLC: checking consensus spec, diameter 12')
print('invariant NoSplitBrain: VIOLATED -> trace: 7 steps (design bug found pre-code)')

title: Signature Alloy relational modeling
description: Signature edition: Alloy models systems as relations and checks assertions within a bounded scope, generating instances or counterexamples automatically. Its analyzer turns 'is my design consistent?' into a SAT problem — lightweight formal methods that fit in a design review.
method: Write signatures and facts; assert properties; the analyzer translates to SAT within a scope; counterexamples are concrete instances.
usage: Model data-structure and access-control designs; check within small scopes; inspect counterexamples as design feedback.

demo.code:
print('Alloy: check NoOrphanedFiles for scope 5')
print('counterexample found: file with no owner -> fix model')
